payload.executive_summary: Branch B01A selects architecture option O1 (sequential staged pipeline) and a conservative, audit-first execution posture. The plan emphasizes deterministic stage ordering with mandatory checkpoints and stage_handoffs, strict separation of powers and role separation (writer/reviewer/judge), and end-of-pipeline “big-bang” acceptance: a single final Freeze Bundle must pass all gates (build/test/lint/typecheck as applicable, integrity, workspace integrity, risk closure, reproducibility, and trace completeness) before anything is considered accepted.

architecture_choice.rationale: O1 best matches the branch’s extremely risk-averse posture by minimizing orchestration complexity and maximizing auditability and determinism. A linear state machine with explicit checkpoints and governed workspace/artifact IO supports the durable audit spine (immutable manifest + append-only event log + versioned artifacts) while making policy enforcement (tool permissions, forbidden/protected paths, op caps, secrets blocking) straightforward and testable. This choice also aligns with the branch’s “big-bang” acceptance strategy: all requirements and acceptance tests are satisfied in one final freeze bundle after holistic review and judgment.
architecture_choice.high_level_dataflow: Intake Gate validates plan_package_final.json + repo_context.json + workspace_context.json → Orchestrator checkpoints and emits Intake→WorkPlanning stage_handoff → Work Plan Compiler produces work_plan.json + trace mapping and checkpoints → Writer Pod produces diff-only patchset artifacts (no direct repo writes) → PatchApply applies patchsets deterministically with forbidden/protected-path enforcement and op caps → Validator Engine runs declared validators and emits test_results.json + quality_reports.json + gate statuses → Reviewer Pod produces findings-only review_findings.json with RFC 6901 evidence pointers → Patcher Pod proposes bounded repairs (RFC 6902 patches and/or replacement patchsets) as needed; orchestrator selects smallest passing repair deterministically → Judge Pod emits trace_report.json + freeze recommendation with evidence-backed decisions → Freeze Assembler runs final integrity/reproducibility/workspace-integrity/trace checks and emits the full Implementation Freeze Bundle + decision_record.json.
key_design_decisions: Use O1 sequential linear state machine to maximize determinism and simplify checkpoint/resume auditing.
Treat stage boundaries as mandatory checkpoints with required stage_handoff artifacts at every transition (no implicit internal transitions).
Enforce strict role separation with reviewers findings-only and judges decisions-only; writers/patchers are the only roles producing patch artifacts.
Adopt end-of-pipeline (“big-bang”) acceptance: no partial acceptance; Freeze permitted only when all closure gates pass in the final bundle.
Deny network by default across stages; allow only via explicit orchestrator policy changes with HITL triggers (if ever required).
Use a single evidence standard everywhere: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer objects into versioned JSON artifacts; forbid alternative citation formats.

milestones.name: Big-bang Implementation Council Plan Package + Freeze Bundle Specification

deliverables.text: Architecture selection and end-to-end staged workflow definition aligned to O1 (Intake → WorkPlanning → Generate → PatchApply → Validate → Review → Judge → Freeze), including checkpoint + stage_handoff requirements at every transition (R4–R6).
Typed/versioned input contracts and schemas: plan_package_final.json intake constraints, repo_context.json schema, workspace_context.json schema (R1–R3).
Typed/versioned output contracts for the full Implementation Freeze Bundle (minimum artifact set and directories) and closure gate validator definitions required before Freeze (R7–R8, R21).

Governance specifications: evidence pointer standard (RFC 6901) enforcement, JSON Patch-only repair model (RFC 6902), diff-only patchset model with deterministic apply/validate loops and forbidden/protected-path enforcement (R10–R15).

Operational governance: tool permission matrix per stage, secrets detection/redaction/blocking guardrails, deterministic retry/quarantine/escalation policy for nondeterministic failures, and role separation + multi-vendor routing constraints (R19–R20, R22–R23).

exit_criteria: All MUST requirements R1–R23 are explicitly addressed in the plan package and are covered by corresponding acceptance tests AT1–AT23 (traceable mapping).

O1 linear pipeline is fully specified as a deterministic state machine with explicit checkpoint boundaries and required stage_handoffs at each transition; no stage transition is allowed without a schema-valid stage_handoff (R4–R6, AT4–AT6).
Freeze Bundle contract includes the complete minimum artifact set and directories and defines validator gates that must pass before Freeze (R7–R8, R21, AT7–AT8, AT21).
Evidence pointers are standardized and enforceable: all canonical artifacts use RFC 6901 pointer objects only; validators are specified to reject any alternative evidence format (R10–R11, AT10–AT11).

Repair/change model is enforceable and bounded: canonical JSON modifications are RFC 6902 patches only; code changes are diff-only patchsets; forbidden/protected-path rules and op/size caps are defined and enforceable (R12–R15, AT12–AT15).
Role separation and governance posture are enforceable in routing and artifact allowlists (reviewers findings-only; judges decisions-only; multi-vendor separation) (R22, AT22).
Secrets policy and nondeterminism policy are specified with deterministic enforcement and logging requirements (R20, R23; AT20, AT23).

decision_log.question: Which architecture option will this candidate use for the Implementation Council workflow?
decision_log.choice: Adopt O1 (Sequential staged pipeline with explicit role pods and a linear orchestrator-owned state machine).
decision_log.rationale: The branch is explicitly conservative and risk-averse, prioritizing auditability and predictability over speed. O1 reduces orchestration complexity (no parallel lanes, no fan-in merge determinism issues) and makes it easiest to enforce checkpoints, tool permissions, forbidden/protected path rules, and append-only audit spine requirements deterministically.
alternatives_considered: O4 (monolithic council component behind a single interface)
what_would_change_this_decision: A hard requirement for parallelism to meet wall-clock constraints, along with a validated deterministic merge/conflict handling design (would push toward O2).
A hard requirement for partial freezes/resumable long-horizon execution under strict budget caps (would push toward O3).
A platform constraint requiring a single internal council service boundary while still exposing explicit stage artifacts and handoffs (might allow O4, with strong internal surfacing controls).

decision_log.question: What is the acceptance posture for this branch: incremental acceptance or end-of-pipeline big-bang acceptance?
decision_log.choice: End-of-pipeline big-bang acceptance: a single final Freeze Bundle must pass all gates and satisfy all requirements/acceptance tests before acceptance.
decision_log.rationale: This branch aims to prevent incremental drift and ensure holistic review under high HITL strictness. Big-bang acceptance matches the linear O1 pipeline and reduces the risk of partial, inconsistent ‘done’ states that complicate auditing and trace completeness enforcement.
alternatives_considered: Incremental acceptance per stage transition (accept parts of the system earlier)
Partial-freeze/resume bundles when budgets are reached (O3-style)
what_would_change_this_decision: If token/time budgets make full completion in a single linear run infeasible and the system requires long-horizon progress preservation, partial-freeze semantics would be needed (would require adopting O3 or extending O1 with partial-freeze).
If stakeholders require early delivery of low-risk changes with strict isolation, a decomposed acceptance model could be introduced with additional governance artifacts and gates.

decision_log.question: How will the workflow enforce checkpoint/resume and prevent hidden state transitions?
decision_log.choice: Treat every stage transition as a mandatory checkpoint and require a schema-valid stage_handoff artifact at each boundary; orchestrator blocks progression if any handoff is missing or invalid.
decision_log.rationale: This directly enforces resumability without relying on agent memory or chat logs, and it strengthens the durable audit spine by making transitions explicit, machine-verifiable, and replayable. It also aligns with the linear O1 execution model and high auditability goals.
alternatives_considered: Allow implicit internal transitions within stages without emitting stage_handoff artifacts
Checkpoint only at major boundaries (e.g., Intake→Generate, Judge→Freeze)
what_would_change_this_decision: If storage/latency constraints make per-transition handoffs too costly, the system could compress handoffs while still preserving required fields and pointers; however it would need compensating validators to maintain resumability and audit requirements.
If a future architecture adopts per-task micro-cycles (O3), checkpoint granularity might become finer (per task) rather than per stage transition.

decision_log.question: What is the authoritative evidence/traceability standard across all canonical artifacts?
decision_log.choice: Use RFC 6901 JSON Pointer evidence pointer objects exclusively; reject any alternative citation formats in canonical artifacts.
decision_log.rationale: A single evidence standard is required for validator-checkable trace completeness, prevention of unverifiable prose citations, and downstream consumption that does not rely on chat logs or non-canonical references. This is central to auditability and to mitigating evidence noncompliance risk.
alternatives_considered: Allow mixed evidence formats (file paths, code pointers, prose citations)
Allow multiple evidence standards per artifact type
what_would_change_this_decision: Only a platform-level change to constraints that explicitly permits other evidence formats; otherwise this remains fixed due to hard constraints and acceptance tests.

If the artifact store cannot support stable JSON-artifact representations of repo/workspace state, the system would need a platform upgrade rather than an evidence standard change (reroute to platform team).

evidence_pointers.quote: All evidence pointers... SHALL use a single standard: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer objects...

evidence_pointers.note: Risk K3 (evidence pointer noncompliance) and mitigation via strict linter validator.
evidence_pointers.quote: Evidence pointer standard ... not used consistently... Add strict evidence-reference linter validator.

decision_log.question: How are changes to canonical JSON artifacts and repository code constrained to ensure deterministic, auditable repair cycles?
decision_log.choice: Canonical JSON artifacts are mutable only via RFC 6902 JSON Patch arrays; repository changes are emitted only as diff-only patchset JSON artifacts with deterministic apply order and bounded apply/validate loops enforced by orchestrator policy.
decision_log.rationale: This combination provides a strictly auditable mutation mechanism, makes repair attempts comparable for deterministic selection of the smallest passing repair, and ensures forbidden/protected-path enforcement can be applied consistently at patch apply time. It directly supports no-silent-scope-expansion and bounded iteration safety.
alternatives_considered: Allow direct JSON artifact replacement writes
Allow tools/agents to edit files directly in the repo workspace
Allow non-diff code mutation mechanisms (e.g., file blobs, prose instructions)
what_would_change_this_decision: If patch application determinism cannot be achieved for a target repo ecosystem, the correct response is to refine patchset format/normalization rules and toolchain pinning (platform work), not to allow direct edits.
If the system introduces a new canonical artifact type requiring a controlled mutation mechanism, it must still be expressible as JSON Patch or it must be treated as immutable and versioned-only.

evidence_pointers.note: Diff-only patchset requirement for code changes.
evidence_pointers.quote: All code changes ... SHALL be emitted exclusively as diff-only patchset JSON artifacts...

decision_log.question: What governance posture is enforced for tools and high-risk operations in this branch?
decision_log.choice: Sandboxed, deny-by-default tool policy with network denied across stages; repo writes only via patch_apply; strict HITL triggers for protected/forbidden paths, secrets, critical security findings, retry budget exhaustion, and any waiver/permission expansion.
decision_log.rationale: This branch aims to mitigate critical governance risks (scope drift, audit spine breakage, policy bypass, secrets leakage) through deterministic enforcement plus high HITL involvement. A conservative tool posture reduces attack surface and nondeterminism, making outcomes more reproducible and easier to audit.
alternatives_considered: Allow network in Generate/Validate by default for dependency fetching
Allow broader repo write permissions during Generate/Patch stages
Reduce HITL triggers to improve throughput
what_would_change_this_decision: If a target repo cannot be built/tested without network access, introduce a tightly-scoped allowlist policy with HITL approval and deterministic dependency pinning requirements (but keep default deny).
If platform sandboxing proves insufficient to enforce path scoping, strengthen enforcement at the patch_apply layer and restrict tool capabilities further (platform/policy change).

synthesis_warnings.summary: Several blocking open questions remain that materially affect enforceability of O1 details (diff format/normalization, artifact_ref naming/versioning, and deterministic ‘smallest passing repair’ selection implementation). Candidate assumes these will be specified by platform/policy to satisfy R13–R15 and related acceptance tests.

Target repo ecosystems/build systems and mandatory vs optional validators are unspecified; without this, repo_context.json validator entrypoints and closure gate defaults (R2, R21) cannot be fully operationalized beyond schema-level definitions.

Workspace backend constraints (size/retention/latency/tenancy) and context-pack bounding/selection rules are unspecified; these impact workspace_index completeness enforcement and deterministic context-pack compilation (R17–R18) and may require policy tuning.
